synthesis: The decay-qualified inverse of the finite difference reconstructs a Hurwitz-zeta eigenfunction from a power-law solution; evaluation at the origin then selects zeta zeros, while the large-x behavior of the differenced state supplies the additional domain filter that removes the trivial-zero sector.
source_support: The source states that Δ has a unit-periodic kernel and only defines its inverse on a decay-qualified class, with a Bernoulli expansion and Borel interpretation. Applying that inverse to the power-law solution gives −ζ(z,x+1), and ψz(0)=0 gives ζ(z)=0. It then contrasts polynomially growing Bernoulli-polynomial states at trivial zeros, for which Δψ diverges, with nontrivial-zero states, for which Δψ tends to zero, and uses this contrast to argue domain exclusion.
nonparaphrase_operation: Composes reconstruction, boundary quantization, and asymptotic domain testing into a two-stage selector: the origin condition discretizes the spectral parameter, but the decay condition distinguishes which selected zeros are admissible.
limits: The inverse is formal and boundary-qualified, some series require Borel summation, and the extracted coefficients, contour data, powers, and operator placement require PDF verification. The asymptotic exclusion is part of a proposed domain argument; no complete domain, bounded similarity, completeness, or self-adjointness result is established.
quality_reason: Three distinct parent units jointly support a concrete dependency unavailable from any one alone: the restricted inverse produces the zeta representation, the origin boundary selects zeros, and asymptotics further filter the zero classes. The synthesis preserves the formal and extraction-sensitive status of the construction.

synthesis: The source combines two conditional routes around the non-Hermitian operator: modified PT symmetry classifies the spectral-reality phase, while a pseudo-Hermitian metric and adjoint eigenstates define a biorthogonal pairing in which the zero-selecting origin condition also removes the integration-by-parts obstruction and makes H formally symmetric.
source_support: The source explicitly labels spectral reality unproved and its analysis heuristic. It makes iH invariant under a modified PT operation and says maximal PT breaking would imply real eigenvalues of H. Assuming momentum is symmetric, it derives a metric relation and formal similarity representatives, constructs adjoint eigenstates and a metric pairing, and then shows that ψn(0)=0 kills the origin boundary term; under that assumption it formally obtains symmetry of H in the new pairing. It later states that the domain, self-adjointness, and completeness needed to justify the adjoint remain open.
nonparaphrase_operation: Relates symmetry-phase classification, metric-induced left-right duality, and endpoint cancellation: the same boundary datum that quantizes the zeta states is reused as the condition enabling formal operator symmetry.
limits: Broken PT symmetry is not shown to be maximal; momentum symmetry and the adjoint identification are assumed; the inverse metric is unbounded; the states have infinite norm; and the orthogonality is distributional and partly RH-conditioned. Completeness, domains, bounded similarity, and self-adjointness are unresolved, so formal symmetry does not prove spectral reality or RH. Formula details remain extraction-sensitive.
quality_reason: The parents jointly support a specific mechanism rather than a thematic association: the metric supplies the dual pairing and the endpoint condition closes the formal integration-by-parts argument, while PT supplies a separate conditional reality criterion. The synthesis retains every stated operator-theoretic and logical qualification.

synthesis: The finite-difference construction approaches a Berry–Keating-type description by two complementary bridges: at fixed difference scale, a similarity map carries Hurwitz-zeta states to power states and transports the origin boundary condition; in a scaled family, shrinking Δε yields a momentum-conjugated dilation operator and the corresponding power-law limit.
source_support: The source defines Δ as a unit shift difference with only a decay-qualified inverse. For a Berry–Keating representative it identifies power-law eigenstates and transports ψz(0)=0 through the similarity relation to a limiting quantization condition involving the power state and Hurwitz zeta. Separately, it replaces Δ by ε⁻¹(1−e⁻ⁱεp), gives rescaled Hurwitz-zeta eigenstates with the same spectral parameter, and states that ε→0 produces p⁻¹(xp+px)p with an x^(1−z) eigenstate.
nonparaphrase_operation: Distinguishes fixed-scale representation transport from scale deformation: one bridge preserves and moves boundary data between operator pictures, while the other isolates the differential dilation core of the discrete-shift family.
limits: Both bridges are formal. The transported limit, scaled-difference normalization, operator order, powers, and proportionalities require PDF verification, and neither the similarity statement nor the ε-limit transports a self-adjoint domain, completeness, boundary control, or rigorous spectral equivalence.
quality_reason: The fixed-scale boundary transport and the ε-deformation are independently present in distinct parents and jointly establish a concrete two-route relation to dilation dynamics. The synthesis does not treat either formal bridge as resolving the source's main domain obstruction.

synthesis: The source deploys a layered diagnostic scheme: growth and non-tempered pairing exclude trivial-zero states from the proposed domain, self-orthogonal Jordan coalescence diagnoses off-critical zeros inside the formal spectral model, infinite norm blocks a Hilbert-space interpretation, and missing completeness blocks identification of the formal adjoint and any self-adjoint realization.
source_support: For trivial zeros the source reports polynomial growth, divergent Δψ, and a pairing too singular to be tempered, whereas the nontrivial sector has better asymptotics and conditional distributional orthogonality. It represents off-critical nontrivial zeros by coalesced eigenstates, Jordan blocks, and self-orthogonality at exceptional points. It separately states that all proposed states have infinite norm, introduces only a tentative cutoff regularization, and identifies the unknown domain and lack of completeness as obstacles to adjoint and self-adjointness claims.
nonparaphrase_operation: Maps distinct symptoms to distinct levels of failure—state-domain admission, distributional pairing, spectral degeneracy, physical normalizability, and infinite-dimensional adjoint justification—rather than collapsing them into a single notion of bad behavior.
limits: The delta pairing assumes the RH-conditioned reality relation, and the exceptional-point conclusions live inside the unproved formal spectral correspondence; neither is independent evidence for RH. The cutoff does not establish a Hilbert-space limit, and completeness and self-adjointness remain open. Several displayed asymptotic and pairing formulas are extraction-sensitive.
quality_reason: Five parent units jointly support a concrete taxonomy with different diagnostic targets and logical strengths. The synthesis preserves the distinction between source-supported exclusions, conditional model consequences, physical-normalization failure, and unresolved operator theory.
